title: Rick Buckler - Wikipedia
notes: Paul Richard Buckler, born 6 December 1955, Woking; died there 17 February 2025, aged 69. Sheerwater Secondary School with Paul Weller and Bruce Foxton; a trainee draughtsman until the Jam's breakthrough. The Jam's drummer from its formation to its break-up in 1982; Time UK (1983), Sharp with Foxton (1986), producing in Islington; a carpenter in Woking in the 1990s; the Gift (2005), From the Jam with Foxton (2007-2009), replaced there by Mark Brzezicki. Autobiography That's Entertainment: My Life in the Jam (Omnibus, 2015).

title: The Jam - Wikipedia
notes: Formed at Sheerwater Secondary School, Woking, 1972; Weller, Steve Brookes and Buckler, then Foxton on bass. Early sets of Chuck Berry and Little Richard covers, then mod: 'Motown, Stax and Atlantic covers'. 18 consecutive UK top-40 singles 1977-1982, four number ones; six studio albums, The Gift a number one. Buckler: drums, percussion (1972-1982).

title: In the City (The Jam album) - Wikipedia
notes: The debut album (Polydor, May 1977); the title track the first single, top 40, May 1977. Buckler on drums.

title: All Mod Cons - Wikipedia
notes: The third album (Polydor, November 1978), produced by Vic Coppersmith-Heaven. Rick Buckler - drums, percussion.

title: Down in the Tube Station at Midnight - Wikipedia
notes: Single, October 1978, number 15; recorded 7 August 1978 at RAK Studios; 'a tense, syncopated beat carried by the bass guitar'; Weller wanted it off the album until Coppersmith-Heaven talked him round. The B-side a cover of the Who's So Sad About Us, Keith Moon on the back cover a month after his death.

title: Setting Sons - Wikipedia
notes: The fourth album (Polydor, November 1979). Rick Buckler - drums; the strings arrangement of Smithers-Jones was his suggestion (Direction Reaction Creation notes).

title: The Eton Rifles - Wikipedia
notes: Single, 26 October 1979, number 3, the band's first top ten; recorded at Townhouse Studios at the third attempt, produced by Vic Coppersmith-Heaven and the Jam. Rick Buckler - drums. His own words on Eton, near Woking: 'these kids were being taught how to fire guns'.

title: Sound Affects - Wikipedia
notes: The fifth album (Polydor, November 1980). Influences include Wire, Gang of Four, Joy Division 'and, particularly evident in Rick Buckler's drumming, Michael Jackson's Off the Wall'; Weller called it a cross between Off the Wall and Revolver. Rick Buckler - drums, percussion.

title: Start! - Wikipedia
notes: Single, 15 August 1980, the band's second number one; built on the guitar and bass riffs of the Beatles' Taxman ('Taxman subconsciously went in', Foxton). The album version 2:30 with trumpets in the last section.

title: The Gift (The Jam album) - Wikipedia
notes: The sixth and last album (Polydor, March 1982), a number one. Weller's new styles 'contributed to a distancing' from Foxton and Buckler, 'uneasy with the move away from the band's former rock and mod revival style'. Rick Buckler - drums; Russ Henderson steel drums.

title: Town Called Malice - Wikipedia
notes: Single, 29 January 1982, number one for three weeks; a 'stomping, Motown-inspired beat' (Greg Freeman, The Guardian); 'a class-war tirade set to a post-punk northern soul groove' (Irish Independent).

title: Rick Buckler (Modern Drummer, April 2008)
notes: An interview from the From the Jam years. Influences: 'There was some really great drumming going on at that time, people like Ian Paice with Deep Purple, John Bonham with Led Zeppelin... They were all a big influence on me'; 'there was no way I could be as good as Ian Paice'. On parts: 'There's no point in trying to copy something. You have to make it your own and leave your mark on it'; 'We did make a specific point during The Jam that we didn't want to get stuck in any musical rut.' On David Watts: 'The original is quite slow, not so beat-oriented.' No kit named.

title: Rick Buckler Remembered (Chris Catchpole, Q, September 2015; MOJO, February 2025)
notes: Weller and Brookes needed a drummer and handed him 'a big stack of albums that were sort of Chuck Berry-style things': 'Go away and learn some of those.' Pub rock (the 101-ers, Dr Feelgood, the Stranglers): 'we felt more at home there'. The band 'always pushing the boundaries of what we could do with a three-piece band'; Start! 'totally different in the way [it was] approached and recorded'. The writer: 'Buckler's tightly-wound playing and bursts of snare gave an electric edge to Weller's songs'; on Tube Station, 'the nervous interaction between Buckler's hi-hat and Foxton's bassline creates a growing sense of dread'; 5 O'Clock Hero's 'melancholy swing'; Funeral Pyre 'his explosive tour de force'.

title: Rick Buckler of The Jam: A Tribute (Steven Valvano, CultureSonar, 22 February 2025)
notes: Self-taught. Buckler: 'I'm not the greatest in the world, but I did take a leaf out of Ringo Starr's book'; 'I realized that the song is the star.'

title: Christie's: Rick Buckler/The Jam drum kit (lot 284)
notes: A five-piece Premier kit in white: snare, tom, floor tom, bass drum, pedal and hi-hat; three Paiste cymbals with stands; used by Buckler in the 1980s. No sizes given.

title: The Jam - Going Underground, Top of the Pops, 27 March 1980 (the band's upload, YouTube 45uSLVE837s)
notes: The kit at 2:00-2:20: chrome-wrapped shells, one tom on the bass drum and a floor tom, chrome stands; Buckler in a dark navy shirt buttoned to the neck, a mod's cut, clean-shaven.
